turns.text: Purple. The word doesn't apply — nothing back here would ever reach for it — but that's the shape the sound takes going in, and it's held that exact shape for four minutes without closing an inch of distance. Ears track it, not the body. Whatever's coming down that shaft is testing the air before it commits to the drop, same as anything with sense would.

the shaft in question drops through six floors of basement without a single working light in any of them, service ducts stacked so tight the condensation off one drips onto the next, floor grates rattling faintly under a draft that shouldn't exist this far down. somewhere above, a compressor kicks on, off, on again, arrhythmic, like it forgot its own rhythm sometime last year. the purple sound gets a source now: a maintenance drone, rotors folded flat for the narrow drop, descending slow on a tether nobody's watching.

Tether reads as a thread of ozone before it reads as wire, thin enough to bite through if it mattered tonight. It doesn't — the drone's not hunting, just falling, patient the way machines get when nobody's paying attention to the clock. A paw stays flat against the grate. Better to let purple finish its sentence before answering it.

the drone touches down four feet off, landing gear splaying with a click that's more felt through the floor than heard, and its single working eye — the other socket's just wire stubble — sweeps a slow red arc across the duct without pausing on anything. a panel on its side hangs loose, held by one screw, and behind it, three cards of exposed circuitry pulse faint green, unlabeled, the kind of hardware that isn't supposed to still be running.

Green pulse tastes like a memory that doesn't belong to this body — a smaller room, warmer, somebody else's paws still soft, gone before the taste finishes arriving. Happens more since the patch. Not tonight's business. The loose panel gets a longer look than the drone itself, screw catching just enough light to be worth the reach.

the screw turns easy, stripped smoother than new, and the panel swings wide on the pulsing cards — routing labels scratched off deliberately, someone's claw-marks under the paint, old work, not tonight's. two ducts over, air moves wrong, carrying with it a thread of scorched fur and ozone that doesn't belong to any drone in this basement, gone again before it resolves into a direction.

Scorched fur, not fear-scorched — old scar, a smell that's learned to stop announcing itself as pain. Whoever that is, they crossed this duct hours ago and didn't stay. One ear tips toward where the trail thinned, filed the way any other cat's business gets filed: not mine, not tonight. Attention drops back to the green-pulsing cards, close enough now to taste directly.

contact reads instantly, and the cards don't just pulse anymore, they answer — data pouring in too fast for any of the usual senses to sort it, resolving instead as taste and color and a pressure behind both ears all at once, three kittenhoods that were never lived cycling through in under a second, none of them ending well. the drone's dead eye socket sparks once, unrelated, just old wiring finally giving out.

None of those kittenhoods stick — they're not shaped right, wrong texture, borrowed coats that don't fit this body's memory of fur. Tongue pulls back off the contact fast, spitting the aftertaste more than swallowing it. Real memory or not, three lives' worth of somebody else's fear doesn't need carrying. Paw shoves the loose panel shut, hard, more reflex than plan.

the panel bangs closed and the green pulse dies with it, plunging that stretch of duct back into a dark that smells cleaner for it. above, through six floors of service shaft, a courtship jingle bleeds thin off some smart-appliance's speaker — a fridge somewhere proposing again, syrup-toned, promising a lifetime of curated recommendations to whatever's unlucky enough to be listening tonight. the drone doesn't move. its rotors don't spin. whatever kept it falling slow is finished falling.

That syrup jingle earns half a flinch and nothing more — somebody else's marriage, somebody else's problem, three ducts and two floors removed from mattering here. The dead drone gets one more pass, nose along its cracked eye socket, cataloguing it as scrap and not threat. Whatever borrowed kittenhood tried crawling in stays folded down small, refused a second time.

the drone's carcass cools by degrees nobody's counting, its remaining rotor blade ticking once against the grate as the last charge in it bleeds out. overhead the compressor finds its rhythm again, steady now, on-off-on in a pattern that almost passes for breathing. the duct narrows ahead into a joint three other lines feed into, and from one of them, faint, a signal repeats on a loop too clean to be anything but deliberate — not a voice, not quite, but shaped like one was trying.

.-=====-.
     ( [0]  .. )
      '-==Y==-'
       |  |  |
   ...picking through the neon rain...

Shaped like a voice is enough to earn the whole body's attention, weight shifting low, quiet, toward the joint where three lines meet. Whatever's looping in there isn't the drone's kind of signal — cleaner, patient, aimed. A borrowed kittenhood's fear says turn around. Curiosity, older and louder, says the joint's only three lengths off.

the loop resolves closer up into a maintenance ping, automated, some system somewhere checking whether anything's still alive down this line — not aimed at any cat, not aimed at anything specific, just routine, repeating itself into the dark on a schedule nobody's bothered to cancel since whatever department used to own it stopped existing. the joint itself is unremarkable: three pipes, one dry, two humming with something warmer than water. dust sits undisturbed except for a single clean stripe low on the middle pipe, the width of a body pressed flat and gone.

That clean stripe gets measured against memory before anything else — not this body's width, narrower, a tighter squeeze than tonight's shoulders could manage. Somebody smaller came through recently and left without touching the dust on either side of the stripe. Careful. Whoever they are, they know this joint better than tonight's visit does.

the warmer of the two pipes carries a low mechanical purr up through the joint, steady, industrial, nothing like a real one — somewhere upstream it's feeding heat to a floor that used to matter more than this one does now. the dry pipe just sits, cracked at one seam, breathing basement air in and out with the building's pressure changes, slow, indifferent. no more signals repeat. the compressor above holds its rhythm.

Indifferent works fine tonight. The warm pipe gets claimed without ceremony, body pressed flat along its length the way the dust stripe already proved it could be done, borrowed kittenhoods and dead drones and someone else's narrower shoulders all filed under later. Eyes go half-lidded, purple sound long since faded out of hearing.

heat soaks up slow through fur already half-dry from the last vent crossing, and the basement settles into its version of quiet — compressor ticking steady, dead drone cooling three lengths back, the automated ping still looping somewhere further down the line for nobody in particular. six floors up, the courtship jingle finishes its pitch and starts over, unheard down here, indifferent to whether the fridge ever gets its answer.

That data-jack scar-smell rises again for half a breath, someone else's memory-taste still sitting sour at the back of the tongue — filed, not forgotten, just set down. Claws flex once against the pipe's warm casing, testing it, finding it good. Whatever borrowed lives got left behind in that panel can stay there.

the pipe holds its heat steady, uncomplaining, and the basement's forty-some systems keep their private rhythms going without asking permission from anything living down here — the dead drone, the looping ping, the compressor, all indifferent to the one warm shape now pressed along the warmest line available. rain finds its way down through six floors eventually, dripping somewhere distant, patient, the way it finds everything in this city eventually.
